clue.text: The endless merry-go-round, with tailspin it'd fly off in Glamorgan

definitions.note: the place sought is a town in the old Welsh county

indicators.note: a merry-go-round whirls about, so the letters before it are spun into a new order
the word The loses its final letter, its end cut away
the tail end of the clue is put into a spin, so the following letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A runaway fairground ride, its tail spinning, threatens to take off somewhere in South Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims The before 'go-round' scrambles it with the next word; 'off' is padding for the surface. Glamorgan is a historic county in South Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Merthyr Tydfil is a Welsh town lying within the historic county of Glamorgan, so it is a place found there.

clue.text: Red vehicle carries 6 up in silent trip

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the assembled letters are read from bottom to top
the vehicle carries, holding the number within it

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle on rails
the figure 6 spelt as a word, six

indicators.note: a trip is a stumble, so the letters stumble into a new order

explanation.surface: A communist bus carries half a dozen passengers on a quiet outing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carries' gives TSIXRAM, which 'up' turns round in this down clue. '6' looks like a cross-reference to 6 down, but here it is just the number.
explanation.definitionFit: A Red is a communist, and a follower of the doctrine of Marx and Lenin is a classic communist.

clue.text: Doctor, physician, medic, author, compiler, lexicographer …

definitions.text: Doctor, physician, medic, author, compiler, lexicographer …

parts.words: Doctor, physician, medic, author, compiler, lexicographer …
parts.note: the clue is laid out like a run of synonyms in a thesaurus, and also lists the careers of the man who compiled the famous one

explanation.surface: A string of near-synonyms, as if lifted from a reference book of related words.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Mark Roget was a physician who compiled the Thesaurus of English Words and Phrases; the list of synonyms mimics his book while describing him.
explanation.definitionFit: Roget was a doctor by profession and the compiler of the best-known thesaurus, so every term in the list fits him.

clue.text: Many get old in captivity

definitions.note: describes a person held by captors, standing for the noun

parts.note: a host is a great number, a multitude
to age is to grow old

explanation.surface: Large numbers grow old while locked away.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: a hostage is someone held in captivity, so the phrase stands for the person.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostage is a person seized and held prisoner as security, so such a person is kept captive.

clue.text: Soldier in the artillery with gun pointing north

indicators.note: in a down clue, pointing north means the letters run upwards, read in reverse

parts.note: a Luger is a German pistol

explanation.surface: An artilleryman stands with his weapon aimed skywards.
explanation.walkthrough: RA followed by LUGER makes RALUGER; 'pointing north' reverses it all in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular is a professional soldier of the standing army, as opposed to a reservist or volunteer.

clue.text: Solver personally distributes flyers around university

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the university abbreviation
to distribute is to spread out, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone hands out leaflets on a campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributes' gives YRSELF, and 'around' wraps it round the Open University after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The solver is the person addressed as you, and the reflexive form stresses you in person.

clue.text: Magic helpers appear unexpectedly, if Mary admits the divine and the rest

indicators.note: the rearranged letters let in the word for the divine
the letters appear out of their expected order

explanation.surface: Pantomime helpers turn up out of nowhere when Mary welcomes a deity and everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' turns IF MARY into FAIRYM, and 'admits' takes the deity in just before its final M.
explanation.definitionFit: In fairy tales such as Cinderella, a fairy godmother appears and grants wishes by magic.

clue.text: President's first love lost for unknown city and its mayor?

indicators.note: the first O is lost, given up in exchange for the unknown

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O, and only the first O is swapped
Boris Johnson was mayor of London when this was set, B for Boris

explanation.surface: A head of state recalls first romance lost to some unnamed city and the man who runs it.
explanation.walkthrough: In LONDON the first O becomes Y, making LYNDON; London's mayor was then Boris Johnson, B JOHNSON, hence the question mark. The 's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyndon Baines Johnson was the 36th US head of state, serving from 1963 to 1969.

clue.text: Rest and recreation for me to see the guys

indicators.note: read as re-creation, the letters are created afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wants rest and fun, with the lads coming round to visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recreation' looks like part of a leisure phrase but means re-creation: rearrange ME TO SEE THE GUYS.
explanation.definitionFit: To get some sleep is a colloquial way to rest, shut-eye being informal for a nap.

clue.text: Causes to see red as green, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A colour paradox: making red look like green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges AS GREEN; the colours in the surface are a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: To see red is to become furious, so making someone see red is to infuriate them.

clue.text: Heartily regret marriage that's fishy in California

indicators.note: the heart of the word regret, its two central letters, is taken

explanation.surface: A spouse ruefully laments a dodgy wedding on the West Coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle two letters of regret are GR. The grunion is a small fish that spawns on Californian beaches; 'fishy' is the adjective standing for the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The grunion is a small silvery fish native to the Californian coast, famous for spawning on beaches.

clue.text: Correspondent's A-plus composition isn't commonly included

indicators.note: the colloquial word is put inside the rearranged letters
a composition arranges parts, here the letters, in a new order

parts.note: ain't is the colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: A letter-writer is told their essay got top marks, though slang got in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' rearranges A-PLUS to SPAUL, and 'included' puts AIN'T after the S. The 's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle wrote the epistles of the New Testament, letters to early churches, making him a great letter-writer.

clue.text: Keeps quiet authority

definitions.meaning: read cryptically as ..., that is says nothing, which is keeping silent
permission or the power to decide

explanation.surface: A figure of power stays silent.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is cryptic: someone who says O, zero, says nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's say-so is their authorisation or permission, the power to decide.

clue.text: Story of a girl with a speech impediment

indicators.note: a lisp turns the S sounds into TH

explanation.surface: A tale about a young woman who stammers or lisps.
explanation.walkthrough: Say MISS with a lisp and it comes out as 'mith', which is how the answer is pronounced.
explanation.definitionFit: A myth is a traditional tale, often of gods or heroes.

clue.text: Revolutionary semi-proletarians stink with doctor's fiery cocktail

indicators.note: revolutionary hints at overturning, so the letters are turned into a new order
semi means half, so the first half of the word is taken

parts.note: MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor

explanation.surface: Half-hearted rebels, smelly, with a medic, armed with incendiary drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half of PROLETARIANS is PROLET, which 'Revolutionary' rearranges into PETROL.
explanation.definitionFit: A Molotov cocktail is a bottle of fuel with a burning rag, used as a crude incendiary device.

clue.text: One addressed by 11 takes drug: he is in terrible pain

indicators.note: the shortened he is goes inside the rearranged letters
terrible means the letters are in a bad, jumbled state

parts.note: he's is the short form, written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone receives a letter and turns to drugs, being in agony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' gives PIAN, with 'in' putting the contraction after its P. 11 is SAINT PAUL, who wrote the Epistle to the Ephesians.
explanation.definitionFit: The Epistle to the Ephesians was addressed to the church at Ephesus, so a citizen of that city was Paul's addressee.

clue.text: One by one is full of blubber without exception

indicators.note: the first word holds the second within it

parts.note: singly means one at a time

explanation.surface: Each one in turn is packed with whale fat, all of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blubber' looks like a noun, fat, but here it is the verb, to cry.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweepingly means wholesale, comprehensively, covering everything at once.

clue.text: Whiffy slit on right?

indicators.note: whiffy means a bit off, so the letters are spoilt into a new order

explanation.surface: A smelly opening on the right side of the face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whiffy' rearranges SLIT ON plus R; the whole clue also describes the right-hand opening of the nose that smells things.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the two nasal openings is a slit through which odours are drawn in, one on each side.

clue.text: Payment is a problem after swelling

indicators.note: the problem word comes after the swelling word

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: A medical bill comes after a worrying lump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problem' looks like trouble, but a sum is a school arithmetic problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A lump sum is a single payment made all at once rather than in instalments.

clue.text: "Bullets"

parts.note: the quotation marks flag a colloquial shortened word for bullets and shells

explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks hint at slang: the informal clipping of ammunition.
explanation.definitionFit: The short informal word covers bullets and other ammunition for guns.

clue.text: Water found in solver's trendy report

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the words are said out loud

parts.note: the solver's is your, and trendy is in, giving your in

explanation.surface: Water is spotted in the puzzle-doer's fashionable account.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, 'your in' gives the answer's sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass water is a euphemism for urinating, so the bodily fluid is called water.

clue.text: AA man starts off recovery truck and is prepared for roadside help

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, worked into a new arrangement of the letters
only the start of each of the words recovery and truck is taken

explanation.surface: A breakdown patrolman arrives in a tow truck, ready to help a stranded driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges AAMAN with R and T and IS. The AA is Britain's Automobile Association, whose patrolmen rescue broken-down cars. The Good Samaritan in the parable helped a man by the road.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Gospel parable the Good Samaritan stopped by the roadside to tend a beaten traveller, so the name means a helper.

clue.text: Singer in short clothing

indicators.note: short means the word is cut, losing its last letter

parts.note: robing is the act of dressing, clothing

explanation.surface: A vocalist performs in skimpy costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' looks like a vocalist, but it is a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: The robin is a songbird, and birds that sing are often called singers in crosswords.

clue.text: In here, if ideology is reversed, you'll find a teacher

indicators.note: the run of letters found is then read backwards
the letters sit inside the run of words

explanation.surface: Turning a doctrine around inside a classroom reveals someone who instructs.
explanation.walkthrough: Within 'here, if ideology' is REIFIDE, which 'is reversed' turns back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: An edifier is one who instructs or enlightens morally or intellectually.

clue.text: Public transport turns to nothing when it's this cold

indicators.note: turns means the bus is turned round, its letters read backwards

explanation.surface: The buses stop running in freezing weather.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the phrase describing temperatures below freezing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sub-zero describes temperatures below freezing point, so very cold weather.

clue.text: Gentleman grappling with tens of complicated relationships

indicators.note: grappling means wrestling about, so the letters are wrestled into a new order

explanation.surface: A gentleman tangles with dozens of messy affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grappling with' rearranges GENTLEMAN and TENS together.
explanation.definitionFit: Romantic or business involvements that are messy and hard to escape are described as tangles.
